sanskrit: tathā mohaḥ pramādaś ca tandrī nidrāprabodhitā kathaṃ cid abhivartante vijñeyās tāmasā guṇāḥ
english: Likewise delusion and heedlessness, languor and the drowsiness that follows from sleep — these, however they may come upon a man, are to be recognized as the qualities born of tamas.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca manaḥ prasṛjate bhāvaṃ buddhir adhyavasāyinī hṛdayaṃ priyāpriye veda trividhā karmacodanā
english: Vyāsa said: The mind sends forth feeling, the intellect performs the act of resolve, and the heart knows the pleasant and the unpleasant — such is the threefold impulse to action.

sanskrit: indriyebhyaḥ parā hy arthā arthebhyaḥ paramaṃ manaḥ manasas tu parā buddhir buddher ātmā paro mataḥ
english: Higher than the senses are their objects, and higher than the objects is the mind; higher than the mind is the intellect, and higher than the intellect, it is held, is the Self.

sanskrit: buddhir ātmā manuṣyasya buddhir evātmano ''tmikā yadā vikurute bhāvaṃ tadā bhavati sā manaḥ
english: The intellect is the self of a man; the intellect is the very essence of the self. When it transforms itself into feeling, then it becomes the mind.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ pṛthagbhāvād buddhir vikriyate hy aṇu śṛṇvatī bhavati śrotraṃ spṛśatī sparśa ucyate
english: By the distinct functioning of the senses the subtle intellect is modified: while hearing it becomes the ear, while touching it is called touch.

sanskrit: paśyantī bhavate dṛṣṭī rasatī rasanaṃ bhavet jighratī bhavati ghrāṇaṃ buddhir vikriyate pṛthak
english: While seeing it becomes sight, while tasting it becomes the tongue, while smelling it becomes the nose — thus the intellect is variously transformed.

sanskrit: indriyāṇīti tāny āhus teṣv adṛśyādhitiṣṭhati tiṣṭhatī puruṣe buddhis triṣu bhāveṣu vartate
english: These men call the senses; and unseen the intellect presides over them. Abiding within the person, the intellect moves among the three states of feeling.

sanskrit: kadā cil labhate prītiṃ kadā cid api śocate na sukhena na duḥkhena kadā cid iha yujyate
english: Sometimes it attains joy, sometimes it grieves, and sometimes here it is joined neither with pleasure nor with pain.

sanskrit: seyaṃ bhāvātmikā bhāvāṃs trīn etān ativartate saritāṃ sāgaro bhartā mahāvelām ivormimān
english: This intellect, whose very being is feeling, transcends these three states, even as the ocean, lord of the rivers, surmounts its mighty wave-tossed shore.

sanskrit: yadā prārthayate kiṃ cit tadā bhavati sā manaḥ adhiṣṭhānāni vai buddhyā pṛthag etāni saṃsmaret indriyāṇy eva medhyāni vijetavyāni kṛtsnaśaḥ
english: When it desires anything, then it becomes the mind. With the intellect one should keep distinctly in view these several seats; the senses, fit to be purified, are to be wholly mastered.

sanskrit: sarvāṇy evānupūrvyeṇa yad yan nānuvidhīyate avibhāgagatā buddhir bhāve manasi vartate pravartamānaṃ tu rajaḥ sattvam apy anuvartate
english: All of them in due order, whatever is not yet brought under control; the undivided intellect abides as feeling in the mind. And rajas, once set in motion, draws sattva too along after it.

sanskrit: ye caiva bhāvā vartante sarva eṣv eva te triṣu anvarthāḥ saṃpravartante rathanemim arā iva
english: And whatever states of being there are, all of them turn upon these three; true to their natures they proceed, as the spokes turn upon the felly of a wheel.

sanskrit: pradīpārthaṃ naraḥ kuryād indriyair buddhisattamaiḥ niścaradbhir yathāyogam udāsīnair yadṛcchayā
english: A man should make himself a lamp by means of the senses, those finest instruments of the intellect, letting them go forth as is fitting, unattached, of their own accord.

sanskrit: evaṃsvabhāvam evedam iti vidvān na muhyati aśocann aprahṛṣyaṃś ca nityaṃ vigatamatsaraḥ
english: Knowing that such is by nature this whole order of things, the wise man is not deluded: neither grieving nor exulting, ever free from envy.

sanskrit: na hy ātmā śakyate draṣṭum indriyaiḥ kāmagocaraiḥ pravartamānair anaye durdharair akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: For the Self cannot be perceived through the senses, ranging amid their objects of desire — senses set upon misrule, hard to restrain, ungoverned by the unperfected.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu manasā raśmīn yadā samyaṅ niyacchati tadā prakāśate hy ātmā ghaṭe dīpa iva jvalan sarveṣām eva bhūtānāṃ tamasy apagate yathā
english: But when with the mind a man rightly reins in their reins, then the Self shines forth, like a lamp burning within a jar — even as, when the darkness has passed, all beings stand revealed.

sanskrit: yathā vāricaraḥ pakṣī na lipyati jale caran evam eva kṛtaprajño na doṣair viṣayāṃś caran asajjamānaḥ sarveṣu na kathaṃ cana lipyate
english: As a water-bird, moving over the water, is not wetted by it, so the man of accomplished wisdom, ranging among objects of sense, is not stained by their faults: attached to nothing, he is in no way defiled.

sanskrit: tyaktvā pūrvakṛtaṃ karma ratir yasya sadātmani sarvabhūtātmabhūtasya guṇamārgeṣv asajjataḥ
english: Having renounced the karma wrought before, he whose delight is ever in the Self, who has become the self of all beings, remains unattached to the pathways of the guṇas.

sanskrit: sattvam ātmā prasavati guṇān vāpi kadā ca na na guṇā vidur ātmānaṃ guṇān veda sa sarvadā
english: It is sattva, not the Self, that gives birth to the guṇas; the Self at no time does so. The guṇas do not know the Self, but He knows the guṇas always.

sanskrit: paridraṣṭā guṇānāṃ sa sraṣṭā caiva yathātatham sattvakṣetrajñayor etad antaraṃ viddhi sūkṣmayoḥ
english: He is the witness of the guṇas, and likewise, in truth, their creator. Understand this to be the difference between sattva and the Knower of the Field, the two subtle ones.

sanskrit: sṛjate tu guṇān eka eko na sṛjate guṇān pṛthagbhūtau prakṛtyā tau saṃprayuktau ca sarvadā
english: The one creates the guṇas, while the other creates them not; the two are by nature distinct, yet they are forever conjoined.

sanskrit: yathā matsyo 'dbhir anyaḥ san saṃprayuktau tathaiva tau maśakodumbarau cāpi saṃprayuktau yathā saha
english: As a fish, though other than the waters, is joined with them, so are those two conjoined; as the gnat and the fig-tree, too, are joined together.

sanskrit: iṣīkā vā yathā muñje pṛthak ca saha caiva ca tathaiva sahitāv etāv anyonyasmin pratiṣṭhitau
english: As the reed-blade within the muñja-grass is both apart and together with it, so these two abide united, each established in the other.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca sṛjate tu guṇān sattvaṃ kṣetrajñas tv anutiṣṭhati guṇān vikriyataḥ sarvān udāsīnavad īśvaraḥ
english: Vyāsa said: It is sattva that creates the guṇas, while the Knower of the Field but looks on. The Lord stands as it were indifferent to all the guṇas as they undergo their changes.

sanskrit: svabhāvayuktaṃ tat sarvaṃ yad imān sṛjate guṇān ūrṇanābhir yathā sūtraṃ sṛjate tantuvad guṇān
english: All this is bound up with its own nature, that it brings forth these guṇas — as the spider spins forth its thread, so does it spin out the guṇas like threads.

sanskrit: pradhvastā na nivartante pravṛttir nopalabhyate evam eke vyavasyanti nivṛttir iti cāpare
english: Once destroyed, they return no more, and no continued activity is found: thus some maintain; while others hold that there is a ceasing.

sanskrit: ubhayaṃ saṃpradhāryaitad adhyavasyed yathāmati anenaiva vidhānena bhaved garbhaśayo mahān
english: Weighing both these views, let a man resolve according to his own understanding; for by this very course one may yet become a great one lying again in the womb.

sanskrit: anādinidhanaṃ nityam āsādya vicaren naraḥ akrudhyann aprahṛṣyaṃś ca nityaṃ vigatamatsaraḥ
english: Having reached that which is without beginning or end, eternal, let a man move through the world neither angering nor exulting, ever free from envy.

sanskrit: ity evaṃ hṛdayagranthiṃ buddhicintāmayaṃ dṛḍham atītya sukham āsīta aśocaṃś chinnasaṃśayaḥ
english: Thus, having passed beyond the firm knot of the heart, fashioned of the intellect's brooding, let him abide in happiness, grieving not, his doubts cut asunder.

sanskrit: tapyeyuḥ pracyutāḥ pṛthvyā yathā pūrṇāṃ nadīṃ narāḥ avagāḍhā hy avidvāṃso viddhi lokam imaṃ tathā
english: As men, slipping from solid ground into a brimming river, are plunged in and suffer, so know that the ignorant are sunk in this world.

sanskrit: na tu tāmyati vai vidvān sthale carati tattvavit evaṃ yo vindate ''tmānaṃ kevalaṃ jñānam ātmanaḥ
english: But the wise man does not founder; the knower of truth walks upon firm ground. Such is he who finds the Self — the pure knowledge that is of the Self alone.

sanskrit: evaṃ buddhvā naraḥ sarvāṃ bhūtānām āgatiṃ gatim samavekṣya śanaiḥ samyag labhate śamam uttamam
english: Having thus understood the whole coming and going of all beings, and rightly considering it little by little, a man attains the highest peace.

sanskrit: etad vai janmasāmarthyaṃ brāhmaṇasya viśeṣataḥ ātmajñānaṃ śamaś caiva paryāptaṃ tatparāyaṇam
english: This indeed is the worth of being born, above all for the brāhmaṇa: knowledge of the Self and tranquillity — that is sufficient, that is the supreme refuge.

sanskrit: etad buddhvā bhaved buddhaḥ kim anyad buddhalakṣaṇam vijñāyaitad vimucyante kṛtakṛtyā manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Having understood this, one becomes awakened — what other mark of the awakened is there? Knowing this, the wise are set free, their task accomplished.

sanskrit: na bhavati viduṣāṃ mahad bhayaṃ; yad aviduṣāṃ sumahad bhayaṃ bhavet na hi gatir adhikāsti kasya cid; bhavati hi yā viduṣaḥ sanātanī
english: For the wise there is no great fear, though for the unwise that fear may be very great; for no one has a goal higher than that which is the wise man's, the eternal one.

sanskrit: lokamāturam asūyate janas; tat tad eva ca nirīkṣya śocate tatra paśya kuśalān aśocato; ye vidus tad ubhayaṃ kṛtākṛtam
english: People resent the world's distress, and gazing upon this and that they grieve over it; but behold there the skilled who grieve not, who know both the done and the undone.

sanskrit: yat karoty anabhisaṃdhipūrvakaṃ; tac ca nirṇudati yat purā kṛtam na priyaṃ tad ubhayaṃ na cāpriyaṃ; tasya taj janayatīha kurvataḥ
english: What he does without forethought of fruit wipes away what was done before; both the agreeable and the disagreeable that come of it, neither does it engender for him who acts thus in this world.

sanskrit: śuka uvāca yasmād dharmāt paro dharmo vidyate neha kaś cana yo viśiṣṭaś ca dharmebhyas taṃ bhavān prabravītu me
english: Śuka said: That dharma than which no higher dharma is found here anywhere, that which is the most excellent of all dharmas — let your honored self declare it to me.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca dharmaṃ te saṃpravakṣyāmi purāṇam ṛṣisaṃstutam viśiṣṭaṃ sarvadharmebhyas tam ihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu
english: Vyāsa said: I shall declare to you that ancient dharma, praised by the seers, most excellent of all dharmas — hear it here with single mind.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi pramāthīni buddhyā saṃyamya yatnataḥ sarvato niṣpatiṣṇūni pitā bālān ivātmajān
english: With the intellect, by effort, restrain the unruly senses, ever apt to break loose on every side, as a father restrains his wayward sons.

sanskrit: manasaś cendriyāṇāṃ ca hy aikāgryaṃ paramaṃ tapaḥ taj jyāyaḥ sarvadharmebhyaḥ sa dharmaḥ para ucyate
english: The one-pointedness of mind and senses is the supreme austerity; it is greater than all dharmas — that is declared the highest dharma.

sanskrit: tāni sarvāṇi saṃdhāya manaḥṣaṣṭhāni medhayā ātmatṛpta ivāsīta bahu cintyam acintayan
english: Having gathered them all, the senses with the mind for sixth, by means of wisdom, let him sit content within the Self, not brooding on the many things that might be brooded upon.

sanskrit: gocarebhyo nivṛttāni yadā sthāsyanti veśmani tadā tvam ātmanātmānaṃ paraṃ drakṣyasi śāśvatam
english: When, withdrawn from their objects, they come to rest within their dwelling, then by the Self you shall behold the supreme, eternal Self.

sanskrit: sarvātmānaṃ mahātmānaṃ vidhūmam iva pāvakam taṃ paśyanti mahātmāno brāhmaṇā ye manīṣiṇaḥ
english: That all-pervading, great Self, like a fire without smoke — those great-souled brāhmaṇas who are wise behold Him.

sanskrit: yathā puṣpaphalopeto bahuśākho mahādrumaḥ ātmano nābhijānīte kva me puṣpaṃ kva me phalam
english: As a great tree, many-branched, laden with flower and fruit, knows not of itself, 'Where is my flower, where is my fruit?' —

sanskrit: evam ātmā na jānīte kva gamiṣye kuto nv aham anyo hy atrāntar ātmāsti yaḥ sarvam anupaśyati
english: so the self knows not, 'Whither shall I go, and whence am I?' For there is another, an inner Self within, who beholds all things.

sanskrit: jñānadīpena dīptena paśyaty ātmānam ātmanā dṛṣṭvā tvam ātmanātmānaṃ nirātmā bhava sarvavit
english: By the kindled lamp of knowledge one beholds the Self through the Self. Having seen the Self by the Self, become free of self, all-knowing.

sanskrit: vimuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyo muktatvaca ivoragaḥ parāṃ buddhim avāpyeha vipāpmā vigatajvaraḥ
english: Freed from all sins, like a serpent loosed from its slough, having attained here the supreme intellect, sinless and rid of fever —

sanskrit: sarvataḥsrotasaṃ ghorāṃ nadīṃ lokapravāhinīm pañcendriyagrāhavatīṃ manaḥsaṃkalparodhasam
english: that dread river, flowing on every side, bearing the world along in its current, infested with the crocodiles of the five senses, banked by the mind's imaginings;

sanskrit: lobhamohatṛṇacchannāṃ kāmakrodhasarīsṛpām satyatīrthānṛtakṣobhāṃ krodhapaṅkāṃ saridvarām
english: choked with the weeds of greed and delusion, swarming with the serpents of desire and wrath, with truth for its ford and falsehood for its turbulence, with wrath for its mire — that foremost of rivers;

sanskrit: avyaktaprabhavāṃ śīghrāṃ dustarām akṛtātmabhiḥ pratarasva nadīṃ buddhyā kāmagrāhasamākulām
english: rising from the Unmanifest, swift, hard for the unperfected to cross — that river, thronged with the crocodiles of desire, cross over by the intellect.

sanskrit: saṃsārasāgaragamāṃ yonipātāladustarām ātmajanmodbhavāṃ tāta jihvāvartāṃ durāsadām
english: It runs to the ocean of rebirth, hard to cross with its hells of wombs, springing from one's own birth, my son, with the tongue for its whirlpool, difficult to approach.

sanskrit: yāṃ taranti kṛtaprajñā dhṛtimanto manīṣiṇaḥ tāṃ tīrṇaḥ sarvatomukto vipūtātmātmavic chuciḥ
english: That river the wise of accomplished understanding, steadfast in resolve, cross over; having crossed it you shall be released on every side, your self made pure, knower of the Self, cleansed.

sanskrit: uttamāṃ buddhim āsthāya brahmabhūyaṃ gamiṣyasi saṃtīrṇaḥ sarvasaṃkleśān prasannātmā vikalmaṣaḥ
english: Resting upon the highest intellect, you shall attain to oneness with brahman, having crossed over all afflictions, your self serene, free from stain.

sanskrit: bhūmiṣṭhānīva bhūtāni parvatastho niśāmaya akrudhyann aprahṛṣyaṃś ca nanṛśaṃsamatis tathā tato drakṣyasi bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prabhavāpyayau
english: As one standing on a mountain looks down upon the creatures below on the ground, so look upon beings — neither angering nor exulting, your mind free of cruelty; then shall you behold the arising and the passing away of all beings.

sanskrit: evaṃ vai sarvadharmebhyo viśiṣṭaṃ menire budhāḥ dharmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha munayas tattvadarśinaḥ
english: Thus, O best of the upholders of dharma, the wise — the sages who perceive the truth — have deemed this the most excellent of all dharmas.

sanskrit: ātmano 'vyayino jñātvā idaṃ putrānuśāsanam prayatāya pravaktavyaṃ hitāyānugatāya ca
english: Having known the imperishable Self, this teaching meant for a son is to be declared to one who is striving, devoted to his welfare, and obedient.

sanskrit: ātmajñānam idaṃ guhyaṃ sarvaguhyatamaṃ mahat abruvaṃ yad ahaṃ tāta ātmasākṣikam añjasā
english: This knowledge of the Self is a secret, the greatest secret of all secrets, mighty — which I have spoken to you, my son, plainly, with the Self for its witness.

sanskrit: naiva strī na pumān etan naiva cedaṃ napuṃsakam aduḥkham asukhaṃ brahma bhūtabhavyabhavātmakam
english: This is neither woman nor man, nor yet is it neuter; brahman, free of pain and free of pleasure, whose essence is the past, the future, and the present.

sanskrit: naitaj jñātvā pumān strī vā punarbhavam avāpnuyāt abhavapratipattyartham etad vartma vidhīyate
english: Having known this, neither man nor woman comes again to rebirth; for the attainment of non-becoming this path is laid down.

sanskrit: yathā matāni sarvāṇi na caitāni yathā tathā kathitāni mayā putra bhavanti na bhavanti ca
english: As all the doctrines are held to be, and yet are not just so, even thus, my son, have they been told by me — they both are and are not.

sanskrit: tat prītiyuktena guṇānvitena; putreṇa satputraguṇānvitena pṛṣṭo hīdaṃ prītimatā hitārthaṃ; brūyāt sutasyeha yad uktam etat
english: Being asked this by a son endowed with affection and with virtue, possessed of the qualities of a true son, lovingly and for his good, a father should speak to his son here what has thus been declared.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca gandhān rasān nānurundhyāt sukhaṃ vā; nālaṃkārāṃś cāpnuyāt tasya tasya mānaṃ ca kīrtiṃ ca yaśaś ca necchet; sa vai pracāraḥ paśyato brāhmaṇasya
english: Vyāsa said: Let him not pursue scents or savors, nor pleasure, nor seek the adornments of this thing or that; let him desire neither honor nor renown nor fame — such is the way of life of the discerning brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: sarvān vedān adhīyīta śuśrūṣur brahmacaryavān ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni na tena na sa brāhmaṇaḥ
english: He may study all the Vedas, attentive and chaste — the Ṛc verses, the Yajus, the Sāman chants — yet by that alone he is not on that account a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: jñātivat sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvavit sarvavedavit nākāmo mriyate jātu na tena na ca brāhmaṇaḥ
english: Though he be as a kinsman to all beings, all-knowing, knower of all the Vedas, if he never dies free of desire, by that too he is not a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: iṣṭīś ca vividhāḥ prāpya kratūṃś caivāptadakṣiṇān naiva prāpnoti brāhmaṇyam abhidhyānāt kathaṃ cana
english: Having performed the various oblations and the great sacrifices with their fees duly given, he does not thereby attain brāhmaṇahood at all without contemplation.

sanskrit: yadā cāyaṃ na bibheti yadā cāsmān na bibhyati yadā necchati na dveṣṭi brahma saṃpadyate tadā
english: When this one fears nothing and nothing fears him, when he neither desires nor hates — then he attains to brahman.

sanskrit: yadā na kurute bhāvaṃ sarvabhūteṣu pāpakam karmaṇā manasā vācā brahma saṃpadyate tadā
english: When he conceives no evil intent toward any being, by deed, by thought, or by word — then he attains to brahman.

sanskrit: kāmabandhanam evaikaṃ nānyad astīha bandhanam kāmabandhanamukto hi brahmabhūyāya kalpate
english: The bondage of desire is the one bondage; there is no other bondage here. Freed from the bondage of desire, one becomes fit for oneness with brahman.

sanskrit: kāmato mucyamānas tu dhūmrābhrād iva candramāḥ virajāḥ kālam ākāṅkṣan dhīro dhairyeṇa vartate
english: Being released from desire, like the moon from a smoke-gray cloud, free of passion, awaiting his time, the steadfast one abides in his firmness.

sanskrit: āpūryamāṇam acalapratiṣṭhaṃ; samudram āpaḥ praviśanti yadvat sa kāmakānto na tu kāmakāmaḥ; sa vai lokāt svargam upaiti dehī
english: As the waters enter the ocean, ever filled yet fixed and unmoving — he who is loved of desires yet desires not desires, that embodied one goes from this world to heaven.

sanskrit: vedasyopaniṣat satyaṃ satyasyopaniṣad damaḥ damasyopaniṣad dānaṃ dānasyopaniṣat tapaḥ
english: The hidden essence of the Veda is truth; the hidden essence of truth is self-restraint; the hidden essence of self-restraint is giving; the hidden essence of giving is austerity.

sanskrit: tapasopaniṣat tyāgas tyāgasyopaniṣat sukham sukhasyopaniṣat svargaḥ svargasyopaniṣac chamaḥ
english: The hidden essence of austerity is renunciation; the hidden essence of renunciation is happiness; the hidden essence of happiness is heaven; the hidden essence of heaven is tranquillity.

sanskrit: kledanaṃ śokamanasoḥ saṃtāpaṃ tṛṣṇayā saha sattvam icchasi saṃtoṣāc chāntilakṣaṇam uttamam
english: The melting away of grief and of the troubled mind, the burning torment together with craving — if you desire purity of being, then through contentment comes the supreme mark of peace.

sanskrit: viśoko nirmamaḥ śāntaḥ prasannātmātmavittamaḥ ṣaḍbhir lakṣaṇavān etaiḥ samagraḥ punar eṣyati
english: Free of grief, free of the sense of 'mine,' at peace, serene of self, the best of knowers of the Self — endowed with these six marks, made whole, he will return no more.

sanskrit: ṣaḍbhiḥ sattvaguṇopetaiḥ prājñair adhikamantribhiḥ ye viduḥ pretya cātmānam ihasthāṃs tāṃs tathā viduḥ
english: By means of these six, endowed with the quality of sattva, wise and high in counsel, those who know the Self after death know likewise those who abide here as such.

sanskrit: akṛtrimam asaṃhāryaṃ prākṛtaṃ nirupaskṛtam adhyātmaṃ sukṛtaprajñaḥ sukham avyayam aśnute
english: Unfeigned, not to be carried off, natural, unadorned — the inner Self: the man of well-wrought wisdom enjoys this imperishable happiness.

sanskrit: niṣpracāraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā pratiṣṭhāpya ca sarvataḥ yām ayaṃ labhate tuṣṭiṃ sā na śakyam ato 'nyathā
english: Having made the mind cease its roaming and established it firm on every side, the contentment that this man attains cannot be had in any other way than this.

sanskrit: yena tṛpyaty abhuñjāno yena tuṣyaty avittavān yenāsneho balaṃ dhatte yas taṃ veda sa vedavit
english: That by which one is satisfied though not eating, by which one is content though possessing no wealth, by which without attachment one gains strength — he who knows that is the true knower of the Veda.

sanskrit: saṃgopya hy ātmano dvārāṇy apidhāya vicintayan yo hy āste brāhmaṇaḥ śiṣṭaḥ sa ātmaratir ucyate
english: For that disciplined brāhmaṇa who, guarding well the gates of his own self and closing them, sits in contemplation — he is called one who finds his delight in the Self.
